title: The Forgotten Ember
premise: In the smog-choked city of Vellamarch, where magic is punishable by the pyre, Kestrel Fairweather survives by stealing memories and bottling them as harmless charms. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into his hands, Kestrel learns it leads to the Ember Vault, where a parasitic spirit called the Hollow King has worn the true king's face for a decade, feeding on the city's warmth to hasten an endless winter. Hunted by the Crown's witch-finders and shadowed by three unlikely allies—a disgraced memory-keeper, a pyre survivor, and a guard who owes him a debt—Kestrel must steal back the real king's memories and return them before midwinter. In the vault's heart he discovers the Hollow King was born from the king's own grief, and that binding it means surrendering his stolen hoard of memories, including his own name. He pays the price: the king wakes, winter breaks, and Kestrel walks out of Vellamarch remembered by no one but the family who chooses to follow him anyway.
about_author: Marguerite Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing letters from people erased from official records, an obsession that bleeds into every page she writes. She lives in a drafty coastal house with too many candles and a firm belief that the best magic stories are about what we refuse to forget.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Kestrel Fairweather works the night market in Vellamarch, selling bottled memories disguised as luck charms while dodging witch-finder patrols. Through his POV we learn the rules of his invisibility: never same customer twice, never a large memory, never stay. The beat is wary comfort—survival as routine, already fraying at the edges.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: A bleeding courier collapses against Kestrel's tenement door and presses a wax-sealed map into his hands, whispering 'the Vault remembers' before dying. POV shifts briefly to the witch-finder Sergeant Hale, who notes the death. The beat is dread: Kestrel realizes the map is warm, alive, and knows his name.

chapters.title: What the Map Wants
chapters.summary: Kestrel tries to burn the map; it refuses to catch fire and instead floods him with a stolen memory of a crowned man screaming in a white room. His POV carries panic and guilt—he recognizes the memory-taste of royal grief. Beat: the past has chosen him, and burning it would mean burning himself.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Broken Things
chapters.summary: Kestrel seeks Odile Vane, a disgraced memory-keeper who once trained him, hoping she can unbind the map. She refuses until she tastes its memory and goes pale: it belongs to the true king, thought dead for ten years. Beat: reluctant alliance; two people who trust no one choosing each other anyway.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Wind
chapters.summary: Introducing Sable, a pyre survivor who lost her magic—and her sister—to the witch-finders, now running a safehouse for the magically marked. Kestrel comes seeking passage out of the city; Sable demands he steal back her sister's final memory from the Crown archive. Beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Debt of Corporal Brann
chapters.summary: Corporal Tam Brann, a city guard whose life Kestrel secretly saved years ago by removing a traumatic memory, catches him breaking into the archive—but covers for him instead. Brann's POV reveals his growing doubt about the Hollow King's decrees. Beat: loyalty tested; the law begins to look like the enemy.

chapters.title: The Archive of Stolen Winters
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Odile infiltrate the Crown archive and find records of a decade of 'voluntary' memory tithes feeding something beneath the palace. They retrieve Sable's sister's memory and glimpse the map's full route to the Ember Vault. Beat: horror and resolve—the thefts were never random; they were harvests.

chapters.title: The Face on the Coin
chapters.summary: Public chapter: the Hollow King appears at the Winter Proclamation, radiant and wrong, announcing an early curfew 'for warmth.' Kestrel watches from the crowd and feels the map burn hotter near the throne. Beat: cold dread made public; the enemy is beloved by everyone.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sable gives Kestrel her sister's memory back and, feeling it whole again, joins the quest outright, bringing the safehouse network as cover. Her POV shows found family forming around shared damage. Beat: warmth kindling against the long winter—literally and emotionally.

chapters.title: Witch-Finders at the Gate
chapters.summary: Hale traces the dead courier to Kestrel's district and raids the tenements. Brann warns them minutes ahead; the group scatters through the rooftops, and Odile is captured covering their escape. Beat: first true loss; survival now costs something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Odile Vane
chapters.summary: Odile's POV under interrogation: she feeds Hale false memories of Kestrel's route while the Hollow King himself visits her cell, tasting her mind and finding the map's echo. Beat: quiet heroism; she protects the family she claimed not to want.

chapters.title: The Road Under the Ice
chapters.summary: Kestrel, Sable, and Brann flee north along a frozen river toward the Vault, pursued by Hale. A blizzard forces them into a cave where Kestrel confesses how many memories he sold—including moments people needed to survive. Beat: confession and forgiveness; the price of his own survival named aloud.

chapters.title: Hale's Doubt
chapters.summary: Hale corners them but finds Odile's planted memories unraveling his certainty about the pyres he's fed. Brann appeals to his oath; Hale lets them go and burns his own warrant. Beat: justice outside the law—an instrument of it choosing conscience over orders.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: They pass a village emptied of all memory of its own names, harvested to nothing by tithe-collectors. Sable recognizes her sister's handwriting on a warning wall. Beat: the stakes made flesh—this is the future Vellamarch is buying.

chapters.title: Doors in the Mountain
chapters.summary: The map leads them beneath Mount Cindral to the Ember Vault's antechambers, guarded by trials that test memory: each must surrender a cherished recollection to pass. Brann gives up his wedding day; Kestrel nearly refuses. Beat: sacrifice as toll; the theme made physical.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Inside, they find the true king, Aldric, alive but hollowed, kept as the parasite's anchor. The Hollow King offers Kestrel a bargain: serve as its new thief and Odile walks free. Beat: temptation sharpened by love; the easiest path is the one that damns everyone else.

chapters.title: What the King Grieved
chapters.summary: Kestrel enters the king's remaining memories and learns the truth: the Hollow King was born from Aldric's grief over a plague winter he failed to stop—it is his sorrow given a crown. Beat: compassion for the monster; the enemy is a wound, not a will.

chapters.title: Odile's Return
chapters.summary: Odile escapes her cell with Hale's help and reaches the Vault as the Hollow King moves to complete the binding of the city. Reunited, the four plan the impossible: return the king's stolen memories and starve the parasite. Beat: the family assembled at last, whole despite everything taken.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: Climax begins: on midwinter night the Hollow King draws the city's warmth for the final binding. Kestrel must pour the recovered memories back into Aldric while Sable, Brann, and Odile hold the Vault doors against the thing's wraiths. Beat: desperate, blazing resistance.

chapters.title: The Price of the Ember
chapters.summary: Climax resolves: the Hollow King cannot be destroyed, only unmade by refusing grief's hunger—so Kestrel feeds it his entire hoard of stolen memories, including his own name and childhood, collapsing it into harmless ember-light. Aldric wakes, weeping and human. Beat: triumph purchased with self-erasure.

chapters.title: A King Made Whole
chapters.summary: King Aldric, restored, ends the tithes, pardons the marked, and disbands the witch-finders; Hale testifies to the harvests. Kestrel, nameless and memoryless, stands apart from the celebrations, unable to feel what he won. Beat: bittersweet dawn; justice achieved, identity spent.

chapters.title: The Names We Choose
chapters.summary: Resolution: Sable, Odile, and Brann find Kestrel leaving the city and refuse to let him go alone—they remember him for him, telling him his own story until he can begin a new one. He takes a new name, Kestrel still, chosen freely. Beat: found family as the answer to everything the world took.
